analysis.evidence: The plural verb agrees with כָּל יְמֵי קֵינָן, “all the days of Kenan.” The numerical predicate עֶשֶׂר שָׁנִים וּתְשַׁע מֵאוֹת שָׁנָה gives their total as 910 years. The verb serves as the copula linking Kenan’s days to that total.
analysis.morphology: Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine plural, with prefixed narrative וַ־.
analysis.sense: to amount to a stated total

analysis.evidence: כָּל יְמֵי קֵינָן means “all the days of Kenan.” The verse gives a single total of 910 years for his lifespan, so כָּל takes the days collectively.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular construct noun, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: כָּל יְמֵי קֵינָן means “all the days of Kenan.” The verse totals those days as 910 years and closes with וַיָּמֹת, “and he died,” so the plural refers to his entire lifespan.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, masculine plural construct, with no prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: (pl.) days of a life, a reign or an age

analysis.evidence: In כָּל יְמֵי קֵינָן, “all the days of Kenan,” the name identifies the man whose lifespan the verse totals as 910 years. The closing וַיָּמֹת, “and he died,” concludes his genealogical notice.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular proper noun in the absolute state, without prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: The personal name of the son of Enosh.

analysis.evidence: עֶשֶׂר שָׁנִים means “ten years.” The following וּתְשַׁע מֵאוֹת שָׁנָה adds nine hundred years, giving Kenan a lifespan of 910 years.
עֶשֶׂר שָׁנִים means “ten years.” These ten years and the following nine hundred years make up כָּל יְמֵי קֵינָן, “all the days of Kenan,” giving his age at death as 910.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, feminine plural absolute, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In וּתְשַׁע מֵאוֹת שָׁנָה, תְשַׁע counts the hundreds and שָׁנָה supplies the unit, yielding nine hundred years. The preceding עֶשֶׂר שָׁנִים adds ten years, giving Kenan a lifespan of 910 years.
analysis.morphology: Cardinal numeral, plural absolute, with no prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: hundreds (plural מֵאוֹת, with the digits: three hundred to nine hundred)

analysis.evidence: In וּתְשַׁע מֵאוֹת שָׁנָה, the singular שָׁנָה supplies the unit for nine hundred. The preceding עֶשֶׂר שָׁנִים adds ten years, giving 910 years as the total of כָּל יְמֵי קֵינָן, ‘all the days of Kenan.’
analysis.morphology: Feminine singular absolute noun, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: After giving Kenan’s lifespan as 910 years, the verse closes with וַיָּמֹת, reporting his death. Kenan is the subject of the singular verb.
analysis.morphology: Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with prefixed וַ־.
analysis.sense: die, come to the end of life
